name: Ashcroft Industries Arc-Flash Coveralls
description:
Flame-resistant coveralls rated for electrical arc-flash events up to 40 calories per square centimeter. The fabric self-extinguishes within two seconds of flame contact and provides a thermal barrier that prevents second-degree burns during high-energy electrical faults. No metal components — every fastener, zipper, and buckle is non-conductive.

Required wear for electrical workers servicing high-voltage infrastructure. Arc-flash events are violent, brief, and catastrophic — temperatures can exceed 20,000°C at the arc point. These coveralls won't save you from a direct arc, but they'll save you from the radiant heat that catches everyone nearby.
functionality: 40 cal/cm² arc-flash rating, self-extinguishing, non-conductive hardware
what_it_says: You work with electricity that can turn air into plasma, and your clothes are the last line between you and that.
story_hooks: Arc-Flash Coveralls show damage patterns from an electrical event that didn't match any equipment at the work site — the arc source was something that shouldn't have been carrying that much current.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian full-body suit with a distinctly industrial silhouette. The coveralls present as a single unified layer from neck to ankle, designed for maximum coverage and mobility. The fabric has a subtle sheen indicative of its technical treatment, and the overall impression is serious, purposeful, and built for survival rather than aesthetics.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso and thighs with articulated seams at joints for unrestricted movement. The arms and legs taper slightly at wrists and ankles to maintain seal integrity when paired with gloves and boots. Cut generously enough to layer thermal undergarments beneath without bulk.
physical_description.primary_material: Aramid-blend flame-resistant synthetic composite with a self-extinguishing topcoat. The base is a dense, tightly-woven ballistic weave treated with ceramic-infused polymers.
physical_description.texture: Smooth to the touch with a subtle grip surface on the palms and inner forearms. The weave itself is tight and uniform, with a matte finish that doesn't reflect light dangerously. Areas of reinforcement (shoulders, elbows, knees) show a slightly raised, quilted texture.
physical_description.color_scheme: Industrial safety orange with high-visibility retroreflective striping in silver running horizontally across the chest, back, and both legs. The orange is a specific arc-flash safety standard hue—vivid enough to stand out in smoke and electrical hazard zones. Dark gray underlay visible at seams.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty ceramic-composite zipper running from crotch to collar with a storm flap secured by friction-fit tabs (no metal). Non-conductive ceramic-resin buttons reinforce the chest. Ankle and wrist cuffs use elastic with drawstring adjustments in aramid cord.
distinctive_features: Embedded thermal monitoring thread woven into the fabric—changes color if temperatures exceed safe thresholds
Reinforced panel zones across the chest, shoulders, and thighs with additional layers of arc-flash rated material
Built-in anchor points (non-conductive D-rings) at shoulders and hip for equipment attachment
Strategically placed venting gussets at armpits and groin to prevent heat buildup during wear
Ashcroft Industries logo embroidered in silver thread on the left chest—subtle but present
Rating label permanently fused to the interior neckline: '40 CAL/CM² ARC-FLASH RATED'
Knee and elbow sections designed to accept optional padding inserts
Dual cargo pockets on thighs with reinforced seams and ceramic-tab closures
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 corporate asset. This is issued equipment, not purchased by individuals. The cost is prohibitive (roughly 8,000 Φ), making ownership rare outside of licensed electrical contractors and corpo infrastructure teams.
physical_description.cultural_context: The wearer is a high-voltage specialist, energy grid technician, or corporate infrastructure worker. Wearing these coveralls signals expertise, hazard exposure, and a job that most people consider too dangerous. The garment commands respect and distance in urban settings.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine or very well-maintained. These are too expensive and functionally critical to be worn casually or allowed to degrade. Users inspect them meticulously before each shift. Minor scuffs and burns on the fabric surface indicate active use but never deep damage—a compromised suit is immediately replaced.
